summary: The paper adapts crosscoders — a recent SAE variant designed for cross-layer feature alignment — to instead align features across pre-training snapshots of Pythia-160M and Pythia-6.9B, then uses decoder norms as a proxy for feature strength over time. Building on this, it documents initialization vs. emergent feature families, a universal directional turning point around step ~1,000, a moderate correlation between complexity and emergence step, attribution-patching circuits for SVA/IOI/induction, and evidence for a statistical→feature-learning phase transition. The idea is a natural and useful extension of crosscoders and the empirical package is reasonably complete for a mechanistic-interpretability contribution, though generality is limited to Pythia and the phase-transition narrative rests on relatively indirect evidence.
strengths: Novel and well-motivated repurposing of crosscoders from cross-layer to cross-snapshot alignment; the argument that the sparsity penalty implicitly drives per-snapshot decoder norms to zero when a feature is absent is elegant and gives a principled evolution proxy.

Multi-angle empirical support: comparison against per-snapshot SAEs (comparable L0/EV, mildly better Pareto), lifetime/steepness/directional-shift statistics, rule-based case studies of previous-token/induction/context-sensitive features, and integrated-gradient attribution patching linking features to SVA/IOI/induction metrics.

The macroscopic observations (KL to unigram/bigram converging while loss approaches token-distribution entropy; total feature dimensionality first compressing then expanding around the ~step-1000 turning point) form a coherent, testable story consistent with prior IB-style predictions.

Limitations section is honest about scope (Pythia only, simple downstream tasks, discrete-snapshot cost), and the theoretical failure-mode discussion (misalignment vs. splitting) shows the authors have thought about the assumptions of their tool.

key_concerns.issue: Generality of the claimed 'universal' training-dynamics findings is supported by a single model family (Pythia) at two sizes, with crosscoders trained at one middle layer each. Claims like 'universal directional turning point' and the statistical→feature-learning transition are stated in model-agnostic language but evidenced only on Pythia mid-layers.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either (a) replicate the turning-point / dimensionality / KL-convergence analyses on at least one non-Pythia open-checkpoint suite (e.g., OLMo, LLM360/Amber, TinyLlama runs) and at multiple layers, or (b) explicitly soften the language throughout (title, abstract, Section 6) to Pythia-specific claims.

key_concerns.issue: The phase-transition argument in Section 6 is largely correlational and could be alternative-explained. Unigram/bigram KL convergence and dimensionality compression-then-expansion coincide temporally with the directional turning point, but no causal/interventional evidence ties them together, and no alternative hypotheses (e.g., learning-rate warmup completion, embedding-norm growth, layer-norm scale changes) are ruled out.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add controls that disentangle optimizer/schedule artifacts from representational reorganization: repeat the analyses on a rerun with a different LR schedule if feasible; correlate the turning point with LR/gradient-norm/embedding-norm curves; and add a direct intervention (e.g., freeze/perturb pre-turning features and measure downstream metric recovery) to move beyond co-occurrence.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical reporting is thin. The complexity-vs-emergence-time correlation is r=0.309 on n=100 features — this is weak, not 'moderate', and depends on a Claude-Sonnet-4 automated rubric whose inter-rater reliability is not reported. No confidence intervals, seed variance, or bootstraps are shown for the ablation/attribution curves, dimensionality curves, or KL curves either.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report CIs / bootstraps for r; validate the automated complexity rubric against human labels on a subsample and report agreement; add seed variance (at least 2–3 crosscoder training seeds) on the key evolution plots (Figures 4, 5, 6b, 7, 8c) so readers can tell if the trends survive re-training.

key_concerns.issue: The 'decoder norm as proxy of feature strength' relies on a sanity check deferred to Appendix C (linear probes), and the alignment-failure discussion is deferred to Appendices A/F. Because these are load-bearing for essentially every downstream analysis, the body currently under-argues them.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Move the core probe-based validation (a small table: probe accuracy for features with high vs. near-zero decoder norm at a given snapshot) and a headline number for feature-splitting frequency into Section 3 or early Section 4.

key_concerns.issue: Positioning vs. concurrent mech-interp work on training dynamics is thin. Prior/parallel efforts to track SAE features across checkpoints (e.g., difference crosscoders for pretrained-vs-chat, per-checkpoint SAE-alignment work cited only in passing) are not directly compared as methodological baselines.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a Related Work paragraph and, ideally, a small quantitative comparison: given the same snapshots, does independently trained per-snapshot SAEs + Hungarian-style feature matching recover the same lifetime/turning-point statistics as crosscoders? This directly justifies the crosscoder choice.

key_concerns.issue: Downstream evaluation is confined to three narrow, well-studied templated tasks (SVA, IOI, induction) on Pythia-160M only. This limits the strength of the 'connecting micro to macro' contribution the paper claims as a headline.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one broader task (e.g., a MMLU-style small subset, or arithmetic emergence à la Nanda et al.) and, importantly, run the attribution patching on Pythia-6.9B as well so the cross-scale story is symmetric with Section 4.

questions_for_authors: How sensitive are the lifetime, steepness, and directional-turning-point statistics to (i) crosscoder training seed, (ii) dictionary size, and (iii) choice of middle layer? Do the same qualitative patterns appear at, say, layer 3 and layer 10 of Pythia-160M?

Can the ~step-1000 directional turning point be explained by learning-rate warmup, embedding-norm growth, or LayerNorm scale changes rather than by a representational phase transition? What do those curves look like overlaid on Figure 5c and Figure 8c?

For the SVA/IOI/induction attribution results, how do the top-k ablation recovery curves compare to (a) random-feature ablation of the same k and (b) ablations using per-snapshot SAE features + post-hoc matching, as a baseline for the crosscoder-specific claim?

Do the feature-splitting cases discussed in Appendix F ever affect the lifetime/turning-point statistics — i.e., could some 'emergent features around step 1000' be splits of pre-existing initialization features rather than genuinely new directions?

How well does the Claude-Sonnet-4 complexity rubric agree with human annotators on a held-out subsample, and does the r=0.309 correlation survive when the rubric is replaced by an independent classifier?
calibration_check: Claims are mostly scoped appropriately (limitations are acknowledged and the phase transition is called a hypothesis), but a few phrasings — 'universal directional turning point', 'moderate correlation' for r≈0.31, and title-level generality about 'language model pre-training' from Pythia-only evidence — modestly overreach the presented evidence.

significance.justification: Extending crosscoders from cross-layer to cross-snapshot analysis is a genuinely useful methodological move for the growing mech-interp-of-training-dynamics area, and the connection to circuit tracing gives concrete downstream utility.

novelty.justification: The core idea — reuse crosscoders across checkpoints and read decoder norms as an evolution proxy — is a natural but non-obvious repurposing; it is more a well-executed adaptation than a fundamentally new mechanism.

rigor.justification: Methodology is coherent and the failure-mode discussion is thoughtful, but several load-bearing claims (decoder-norm-as-strength, alignment quality, phase transition) rest on appendix-level checks or correlational evidence rather than in-body interventions.

statistical_soundness.justification: Effect sizes are under-reported: r=0.309 is labelled 'moderate', no CIs/bootstraps on the evolution curves, no seed variance for crosscoder training, and the LLM-judge complexity rubric is not validated against humans.

calibration_honesty.justification: Limitations section is candid about scope, and Section 6 frames its claims as a hypothesis; a few remaining phrasings ('universal', 'moderate correlation', title-level generality) mildly overshoot.

clarity.justification: Structure and notation are readable and the method is explained precisely, but the prose is dense in places, several key checks are deferred to appendices, and OCR-style spacing artifacts in the extraction hint at some presentation roughness in the body.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard ICLR structure — Introduction, Related Work, Method, Assessment, Circuits, Phase-Transition observations, Limitations, Conclusion — is followed cleanly and at a reasonable length.

reproducibility.justification: Pythia snapshots, SlimPajama, layer choices, snapshot sampling, crosscoder architecture, loss, and attribution-patching details are all described concretely enough to reimplement, though key hyperparameters (dictionary sizes, λ_sparsity schedules, IG steps) rely on appendix content not fully visible here.

related_work.justification: Covers SAEs, crosscoders, NTK/IB/SLT, and prior circuit-tracing work, but positioning against concurrent efforts to track SAE features across training and against per-snapshot-SAE+matching baselines is thin.

figure_quality.justification: From the captions, the figure set is well-designed to support the argument (crosscoder-vs-SAE Pareto, lifetime/steepness/direction statistics, attribution ablations, KL and dimensionality curves) — each display item maps clearly to a claim.

breadth_generality.justification: Evidence comes from one model family (Pythia) at two sizes, one middle layer per model, one dataset (SlimPajama), and three templated tasks — insufficient to support the model-agnostic language used for the headline findings.

overall_recommendation.justification: A useful, empirically rich mech-interp-of-pretraining paper with a clean methodological hook and honest limitations, held back from a clear accept by narrow generality, weak-to-moderate statistical support for headline claims, and the largely correlational nature of the phase-transition argument.
